questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some coolers are mixers. Some mixers are scissors. Some scissors are knives. Conclusions: I. Some knives are mixers. II. Some scissors are coolers. III. Some knives are coolers. IV. No knife is a mixer.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some coolers are mixers.

Some mixers are scissors.

Some scissors are knives.

Conclusions:

I. Some knives are mixers.

II. Some scissors are coolers.

III. Some knives are coolers.

IV. No knife is a mixer.

options.text: Only conclusions III and IV follow
options.html: Only conclusions III and IV follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and IV follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and IV follow

questions.solution:
I. Some knives are mixers. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between knives and scissors. Hence, false)

II. Some scissors are coolers. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between coolers and scissors. Hence, false)

III. Some knives are coolers. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between knives and coolers. Hence, false)

IV. No knife is a mixer. → Does not follow (There is no definite relation between knives and mixer. Hence, false)

Hence, ‘None of the conclusions follow’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: The present age of Rahim is five times the present age of his daughter, Savita. Seven years from now, Rahim will be three times as old as Savita. What is the present age (in years) of Rahim?
questions.questionHtml: The present age of Rahim is five times the present age of his daughter, Savita. Seven years from now, Rahim will be three times as old as Savita. What is the present age (in years) of Rahim?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Rahim to Savita age: Present = 5 : 1, After 7 years = 3 : 1.

Make the ratio difference equal: Present (5:1, diff 4) → 5:1. After 7 yrs (3:1, diff 2) × 2 → 6:2.

Increase in ratio unit: 6 − 5 = 1 unit. Since 1 unit = 7 years.

Rahim's present age = 5 units = 5 × 7 = 35 years.

∴ The correct answer is 35 years.

Alternate Method

Given: Present ratio = 5:1. After 7 years ratio = 3:1.

Formula: Age after n years = Present age + n.

⇒ Let Savita's present age be x. Then Rahim's present age = 5x.

⇒ After 7 years: (5x + 7) = 3 × (x + 7)

⇒ 5x + 7 = 3x + 21

⇒ 5x − 3x = 21 − 7

⇒ 2x = 14

⇒ x = 7 years.

⇒ Rahim's present age = 5 × 7 = 35 years.

∴ The correct answer is 35 years.

Additional Information

Ratio Difference Method

To solve age problems quickly, ensure the numerical difference between ratio parts remains constant by multiplying with the cross-difference of the other ratio.

Age Invariance

The difference between the ages of two people always remains the same, regardless of how many years pass.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.

B. I am especially proud of it, not only because it has survived several winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.

C. The tree had grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.

D. Last summer, I spent many days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "DCBA."

  • The paragraph is about the author's prized peach tree and their observations of it during the summer.
  • The correct order of the sentences is:
    • 1.D - mentions the subject of the passage and explains the author's observations of ants on the tree.
    • 2. C - describes the location and growing conditions of the tree.
    • 3. B - expresses the author's pride in the tree's survival and productivity.
    • 4. A - describes the author's observation of the tree's leaves withering during the summer.
  • Thus, the correct order will be "DCBA."

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.
